I've been farming this same land in Quzhou for 10 years now. Cotton is all I know — my father grew it, I grow it, and it's what the traders around here buy. With 10.1 mu, there's no point splitting into something else. My wife and brother-in-law work in the city part of the year, so the pressure isn't as heavy as it used to be, but I still need this crop to perform. If I switch to something new and fail, I lose everything for the season.

I'll plant all 10.1 mu in cotton this spring, same as always. I buy hybrid seeds from the cooperative in town — I switched to hybrid about four years ago after seeing my neighbor's yields jump, and I haven't gone back. My soil is okay but not rich, so I'll put down a solid base of fertilizer before planting: roughly 15 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu. I split the nitrogen — half as base, half as top-dressing when the bolls are setting. I've learned not to overdo the early nitrogen or the plants get too leafy.

My well gives me good control over irrigation. I'll water 4 times: once before planting to ensure good germination, once during seedling establishment if it's dry, once at flowering, and once during boll development. That's usually enough here unless we get a drought year.

For pests — cotton is a nightmare for pests. Aphids, bollworms, whiteflies. I'll spray around 10 times through the season. I know that sounds like a lot but if I skip a spray and bollworm hits, I can lose a third of my yield. I use rotary tillage before planting to break up the compaction from last year.

I expect around 290 kg of seed cotton per mu. That's what I usually get with decent weather.
